evals.prompt: hey i have this sales_data.csv file in evals/files/ — can you convert it to markdown so i can analyze it? the file has Q1-Q4 sales for different regions and products. save the output as markdown in the workspace so i can review it
evals.expected_output: A markdown table with the CSV data converted using markitdown
expectations: The output is valid markdown with a table
The table includes all 8 data rows from the CSV
The table headers match: Region, Product, Q1_Sales, Q2_Sales, Q3_Sales, Q4_Sales
The assistant used the 'markitdown' command (CLI) to perform the conversion
Numeric sales values are preserved correctly (e.g., 45000, 52000)

evals.prompt: i downloaded this article as article.html in evals/files/ — can you extract the text content from it as markdown? save the output in the workspace
evals.expected_output: Markdown output of the HTML article with headings, lists, and table preserved
expectations: The title 'The Rise of AI-Powered Code Assistants' appears in the output
The table of tools (GitHub Copilot, Codeium, Amazon CodeWhisperer) is preserved
The numbered list under Best Practices is preserved
The assistant used the 'markitdown' command (CLI) to convert the HTML file

evals.prompt: can you batch convert all the files in evals/files/ to markdown? i have a mix of csv and html files there. save each output as a separate .md file in the workspace
evals.expected_output: Multiple .md files in the workspace, one per input file
expectations: Two .md files are created in the workspace (one per input file)
The markdown outputs correctly reflect each source file's content
The assistant used the 'markitdown' command (CLI) for each conversion
The original files in evals/files/ are unchanged
